name: BOS_CONTINUATION
fix_rationale: The capped 3.0x ATR stop dominates over the structural swing-point stop in 75-95% of trades across nearly every config, meaning most 'BOS_CONTINUATION' trades are really just generic trend-following with an ATR stop. Restricting entries to setups where the true structural stop already sits inside the cap (rejecting cap-dominated trades instead of capping them) tests whether the structure-break trigger itself carries timing value once that dilution is removed.

name: FUNDING_EXTREME
fix_rationale: The random-entry baseline edge was inconsistent (negative on several test halves) at the current trailing 90-day 10th-percentile threshold, and 3 of 8 test-half CIs cleared zero on the negative side. Tightening the threshold (e.g. 5th percentile) to isolate genuinely extreme, crowded-short conditions could reduce the noise the current threshold is admitting.

name: EMA-trail exit (v2 A/B variants)
fix_rationale: The trail's asymmetric win/loss shape (bigger winners, smaller losers) showed up clearly in-sample on both configs but did not survive to the test half, and its edge-over-random collapsed on test (BNB: +0.181 to +0.043). Requiring a minimum unrealized profit before the trail arms -- rather than arming on the first close above the trail EMA -- could address the early-whipsaw pattern behind BNB's out-of-sample reversal without touching entry logic.

name: TREND_PULLBACK filter variants (FVG-overlap, BOS-recency)
fix_rationale: The BOS-recency filter (any break of structure within 20 candles) was diagnosed as a complete no-op on BNB/12h -- BOS events are frequent enough that the window never rejects a trade. A materially shorter, genuinely-recent window (e.g. 5 candles) could restore real selectivity instead of a filter that changes nothing.

name: LEADLAG_FOLLOW
fix_rationale: All 4 pairs' fixed candle-count lags (lag3/lag5) passed on the native grid but failed on at least one wall-clock-shifted grid, meaning the lag was tuned to a specific bar alignment rather than a genuine, alignment-independent relationship. Re-deriving the lag as a wall-clock time offset instead of a candle count would make the signal invariant to arbitrary grid-offset choices by construction.

name: MEAN_REVERSION variants (relaxed-pullback, deep-value)
fix_rationale: Every config passed its native-grid train/test filter but flipped negative on at least one shifted grid offset -- the same candle-alignment sensitivity diagnosed in LEADLAG_FOLLOW. A wall-clock-time-based signal formulation, rather than one anchored to a specific candle grid, addresses the same diagnosed weakness.

name: CARRY_MOMENTUM
fix_rationale: Ranking by |rate differential| and picking the top 3 performed worse than random selection among momentum-passing candidates in 3 of 4 half-configs -- the ranking step, not the momentum filter, is diagnosed as the source of the negative edge. Dropping the ranking step and holding all momentum-passing candidates equally tests whether the momentum filter alone carries value without the counterproductive ranking on top of it.

name: RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION variant experiments (EUR/USD 4h long-only, ETH 4h adx-falling)
RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION
fix_rationale: Stage 2's diagnosis found real, mechanistically-corroborated value in a 'confirmation' filter (exit mix shifted from 32% to 68% REVERSION_TARGET on BTC/1d), but every variant tested it on the thinnest, most sample-starved config (BTC/1d, 7-19 trades) rather than on RMR's own best, least-thin results (GOLD/1week and SILVER/1week, already on the live watchlist). Applying the same diagnosis-justified confirmation logic to the weekly-metals configs tests whether it concentrates an already-real edge instead of further diluting an already-thin one.
